question: Should Microsoft Teams adopt `channels.msteams.accounts` plus `defaultAccount` as a supported multi-bot configuration contract?
rationale: The patch is technically sound, but it creates a new public setup, routing, credential, authorization, and state model that requires maintainer sponsorship rather than reviewer inference.

options.title: Sponsor the account model
options.body: Accept the standard account/default/binding shape after removing unrelated glossary churn and satisfying exact-head gates.

options.title: Narrow the first landing
options.body: Split advanced Graph, SSO, setup, or state surfaces if maintainers want a smaller initial compatibility contract.

options.title: Decline the feature direction
options.body: Close the PR and linked request if OpenClaw does not want multiple Teams bot identities per gateway.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the account model
recommendation.body: Accept the standard account/default/binding shape after removing unrelated glossary churn and satisfying exact-head gates.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent history across Teams/config, authored security-sensitive Teams changes, and were directly requested on this PR.
